whatItFakes: The Campaigns tab lists the coming ballot's races with who runs and their filed stances, and a candidate's name opens their card; the owner's 'clicking a candidate's rally lets you go there and learn their views' has no rally to go to, so there is no rally link.
why: No engine keeps a candidate's rallies as events with a place and a time: the campaigns module holds filings, contests, bills, stories, terms and ties, and the director's rally-opponent situation fires from a paid message or a debate, never from a place the player travels to.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: A campaign event record (a rally with its venue, date and speaker) the director stages as a scene the player can travel to from the race's row, where the candidate's views are heard; the row then links to it.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: A filing made at the counter carries no platform: the rules panel's stance form is gone (owner, Oct 28, point 31) and the filing's platform is empty until the elections engine reads the filer's own views.
why: fileCandidacy takes the platform as handed in; nothing derives it from the person's own policy views (the records the party fit reads), so without the form there is nothing to hand in.
replacement: fileCandidacy derives the platform from the filer's own view records on each of the contest's positions when none is handed in; the Campaigns row then reads those stances.

whatItFakes: The filing counter offers at most four replies; an office that takes more races than that shows the four soonest at the counter, and the rest are reached from the office's own view in Travel and from Campaigns.
why: The talk box holds a few replies, never a long list (owner, Oct 26), and the Open races menu that held the rest was a dev panel (owner, Oct 28, point 29).
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: The clerk asks which race in the conversation (the words session's clerk lines, point 32) and the counter opens on the race chosen in Travel or Campaigns, so no list is needed at the counter.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: Hovering a race at the counter shows a card on the office with what the records know (its district, the election day, who holds the seat); it does not yet say what the office does in words.
why: No record or bank holds a line per office kind on its duties; words typed into the screen would be hand-written player text.
replacement: An office-duties bank from the words session (one piece per office kind, graded like every bank) that the hover card reads first, the record's facts after it.

whatItFakes: The Metrics tab's town figures (people at work, people looking for work, jobs open, rental homes, empty rentals, typical rent and home value, people claiming unemployment now), and its state figures from the second year of play, show the current value only, with no 'last year' beside them. Evictions count only households that are full people (a counted household's case names no town).
why: The jobs engine keeps no year-ago reading of its counts, the town's monthly metrics months are empty until the world has run, and the regional engine keeps only its last twelve months and each December, so after the first year there is no state row for the month a year before. Only the national months and the opening's drawn history carry a year-ago reading. The housing stock keeps only the opening's typical rent and home value, the jobs claims keep no year-ago count, and an eviction case names a household, not a town.
replacement: The world-metrics module keeping the town's monthly numbers from the opening, and the regional engine keeping the month a year before each month it shows, so every figure has last year beside it; the Metrics screen already reads this year and last as two columns.

whatItFakes: News puts first the local outlets the player follows this week (press.ts followersOf), else the town's paper of record (townOutlet), and keeps that order while the game is open; the press settles who follows what weekly by lean, so a player who changes papers sees the change only after reopening the game, and nothing records that a household subscribes.
why: play-nov8-news-opens-on-a-different-paper-each-time asks News to open on the paper the household follows and keep it while the game is open; the press keeps followers per person, settled weekly, not a household subscription that holds.
replacement: A press-engine record of the outlets each household reads, kept steady from week to week (subscriptions by household, set by its own habits and money; followersOf as its start), which News reads to choose the paper in front.
